paragraphs.text: Lesson 27, bad habits.
Mandy wants her boyfriend Toby to get rid of some bad habits.
Listen to their conversation as you try to answer the comprehension questions.
Will you stop biting your fingernails? It's so gross.
Hey, Valley Girl. This is Texas, not Los Angeles.
Here in Texas, a guy can bite his nails.
I'm not asking you to get a manicure. I just want my boyfriend to have decent looking hands.
Your fingernails have these ragged edges. They look like they've been gnawed on by a rodent.
Doesn't bother me? Besides, hands are made for working.
Heck, you know, cow looking at my fingernails when I'm doing the milking.
We're not on your farm, Toby, so get with the program.
Next week my friends' melee are driving here to see me.
If they see your nasty fingernails, they'll think you're a slob, like for sure.
Look, I'm a farmer and darn proud of it.
And if I want to bite my fingernails, I will.
It's not like I chew my bottom lip like you do.
What's that supposed to mean?
Ah, come down off your eyes, horse.
You're always biting your bottom lip like it's a juicy steak or something.
What's the matter? The sari stick you ate for breakfast wasn't enough for you?
Hey, I don't want to hear any of your snide comments about my weight.
All I'm saying is that you got your vices too, so don't fuss about mine.
You're hopeless. Biting your nails is like a habit most people grow out of by the time they're 10.
It's about time you stopped.
It's about time you stopped chewing on your lip. You're doing it right now.
Okay, fine. It's a bad habit, but so is biting your nails.
Yeah, but there's a lot of worse ones. Like cussing and chewing tobacco and hitting the bottle like my old man does.
But I don't do any of those. I just bite my fingernails when I get aggravated or stressed. That's all.
That's the same reason I chew on my lower lip. I don't even realize I'm doing it.
Okay, fine. Let's make a deal. Whenever we feel the need to bite a fingernail,
or chew on a lip, we'll just talk to each other instead. Deal?
Deal. I knew there was a reason I liked you, but you still need a makeover, farmer boy.
I'll never hear the end of it if my friends see you in those grubby overalls.
Oh, good grief. Here we go again.
Let's learn the expressions from Mandy and Toby's conversation.
Mandy says that Toby's habit of biting his fingernails is so gross. The word gross means disgusting.
She says, I'm not asking you to get a manicure. I just want my boyfriend to have decent looking hands.
The word manicure refers to getting your nails professionally cleaned and decorated.
Toby's fingernails have ragged edges. This means that the edges of his nails are uneven as though
they were torn instead of cut. Mandy says they look like they've been gnawed on by a rodent.
Nawed on means chewed and a rodent is a rat or another similar animal.
Toby says this doesn't bother him because hands were made for working.
Then he says, heck, ain't no cow looking at my fingernails when I'm doing the milking.
The word ain't is a very informal word for there isn't or there aren't.
But Mandy replies, we're not on your farm Toby, so get with the program.
Get with the program means follow the rules and do what you're supposed to do.
Mandy's friends are coming to visit her and she says if they see your nasty fingernails
they'll think you're a slob. The word nasty is another word for disgusting.
And a slob is a dirty, messy person who doesn't take care of themselves.
Toby accuses Mandy of having bad habits as well. He says, come down off your high horse.
This expression means don't act so superior. Mandy's bad habit is biting her bottom lip
like it's a juicy steak. A juicy steak is a piece of meat that's full of liquid.
And Toby makes a sarcastic comment about what Mandy ate for breakfast.
Mandy replies, hey, I don't want to hear any of your snide comments about my weight.
A snide comment is a sarcastic and insulting comment.
Toby replies, all I'm saying is that you've got your vices too, so don't fuss about mine.
A vice is a terrible habit or addiction. And fuss means to worry and complain.
Mandy thinks Toby is hopeless. Your hopeless means there's no hope or possibility of you changing
or improving. According to Mandy, biting your nails is a habit that most people grow out of by the
10. To grow out of something means to stop doing it as you grow up and become more mature.
Then Mandy says, it's about time you stopped. The expression it's about time means this should
have happened a long time ago. Toby points out that there are a lot of worse habits like cussing.
Cussing is swearing using bad language and hitting the bottle.
Hitting the bottle is a slang way to say drinking alcohol. Toby says, hitting the bottle like my
old man does. My old man is a slang way to say, my father. Toby bites his fingernails when he gets
aggravated or stressed. The word aggravated means very annoyed. Toby and Mandy make a deal to talk
to each other instead of indulging in their bad habits. But at the end of the conversation,
Mandy says that Toby still needs a makeover. A makeover is a complete change and a complete
improvement of your appearance. Mandy says, I'll never hear the end of it if my friends see you in
those grubby overalls. I'll never hear the end of it means I'll constantly be reminded of this by
someone. In other words, if Mandy's friends see Toby's clothes, they'll constantly tease and
remind her about it. Especially those grubby overalls. The word grubby means worn out and dirty.
And overalls are a type of pants with straps that go over the shoulders.
Overalls are often worn by farmers and you can click the link in the text lesson to see a picture.
That's all the vocabulary from today's conversation. Go ahead and try the vocabulary quiz to put these
expressions into practice and the speaking task to get some feedback on your spoken English.
